senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; cmp. חֲרַשׁ) [closed up,] deaf, dumb (cmp. אִלֵּם); deaf and dumb.
units: Ter. I, 2 ח׳ שדברו וכ׳ the ḥeresh of which the scholars speak (in a legal sense) means everywhere deaf and dumb.
Ib. ח׳ המדבר וכ׳ a ḥeresh that can talk but not hear.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 2:4">Meg. II, 4</cite> <he>חוץ מח׳</he> except a deaf person.

<cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 153:8">Sifré Num. 153</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 30:5">Num. XXX, 5</cite>; <cite ref="Numbers 30:12">12</cite>) <he>להוציא את הח׳</he> this excludes the case of the father (the husband) being deaf; <cite ref="Nedarim 73a:2">Ned. 73ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>חֵרְשִׁים</he>, <cite ref="H01789"><he>חֵרְשִׁין</he></cite>.
Ruth R. s. 2 beg. (ref. to חרש, Josh. II, 1) עשו עצמכם ח׳ pretend to be deaf.—Fem. חֵרֶשֶׁת.
